quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When riding in a group and taking a curve, what formation should you use?

options.text: A single-file formation.
Pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to be seen is to keep your headlight on and use running lights if you have them. Use your high beam during the day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake and then re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the front brake pressure right away. Then re-apply the brake slowly and steadily.

questions.question: During a normal turn, which way should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: In the same direction.
In opposite directions.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body upright.

questions.question: What should you do if you shift gears while in a curve?

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
Shift in the curve instead of before it.
Shift gears to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, shift smoothly. A sudden change in engine power can cause the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, what should you always do?

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly look in the rearview mirror.
Check your rearview mirror often.
Do not use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while riding. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and helps drivers in the next lane see your move.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of staying a safe distance from other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to the movements of other drivers.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Staying a safe distance from other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely. This increases your escape route options, not limits them.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides good traction for riding, except when it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction for riding, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but provides adequate traction for riding in dry conditions. In rain, avoid it. The strip is typically about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of your lane.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good road surface, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can maintain control of your motorcycle as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight within your lane to cross angled railroad tracks. Changing your angle may push you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointed with your toes aiming downward.
Relaxed.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Perform both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Perform one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look downward to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so other drivers see you are slowing down. This is especially important when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns or curves.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns or curves.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and downshift. As the dog gets close, accelerate and pull away from it.

questions.question: When should you keep a larger distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Slippery roads, heavy traffic, or limited visibility all require a larger following distance. Use at least a four-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: How far before a turn should a motorcyclist signal?

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
150 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal a left or right turn 100 feet before you turn. This gives other drivers time to see your signal and react safely.

questions.question: On a highway, how long before changing lanes should a motorcyclist signal?

options.text: Two seconds
Five seconds
10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Five seconds
questions.explanation: On the highway, signal a lane change at least five seconds ahead. This gives other drivers time to see your signal and react safely.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more distance to stop.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. A good rider adjusts their position for safety.
